payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-02
payload.summary:
English: Today’s snapshot covers 14 X/Twitter builders and one podcast episode. The X posts center on **Codex**, AI agent workflows, enterprise AI strategy, model distribution, **Vercel** agent evaluations, and founder operating tactics. The podcast item summarizes **Unsupervised Learning**’s discussion with **Sebastian Mallaby** about **Demis Hassabis**, **DeepMind**, AI race dynamics, and government-led safety coordination.

中文：今天的快照包含 14 位 X/Twitter builder 和 1 期播客。X 内容集中在 **Codex**、AI agent 工作流、企业 AI 策略、模型分发、**Vercel** agent 评测，以及创始人的实操方法。播客部分总结了 **Unsupervised Learning** 与 **Sebastian Mallaby** 关于 **Demis Hassabis**、**DeepMind**、AI 竞赛格局和政府主导安全协调的讨论。

sections.headline: **Unsupervised Learning** unpacks **Demis Hassabis**, **DeepMind**, and the AI race · **Unsupervised Learning** 拆解 **Demis Hassabis**、**DeepMind** 与 AI 竞赛
sections.body:
The episode features **Sebastian Mallaby**, who spent extensive time with **DeepMind** CEO and cofounder **Demis Hassabis** while writing *The Infinity Machine*. The conversation covers **DeepMind**’s early hope of avoiding an AI race, why Mallaby now sees the race dynamic as inevitable, and how Hassabis shifted from a possible singleton-lab vision toward seeing safety as a collective action problem that governments must enforce.

这一期请到 **Sebastian Mallaby**，他在写 *The Infinity Machine* 时与 **DeepMind** CEO 兼联合创始人 **Demis Hassabis** 深谈过很长时间。节目讨论了 **DeepMind** 早期想避免 AI 竞赛的设想、Mallaby 为什么认为竞赛几乎不可避免，以及 Hassabis 如何从“单一实验室掌控局面”的想法，转向把安全视为必须由政府执行的集体行动问题。

Mallaby also discusses the 2015 safety summit hosted at **SpaceX**, **Elon Musk**’s later move to start **OpenAI**, the trust problem between AI labs, and why he thinks enforceable rules would need both domestic technical institutions and some form of **US-China** coordination. He points to the UK AI Safety Institute as evidence that governments can assemble serious technical expertise, while noting the difficulty of international coordination.

Mallaby 还谈到 2015 年在 **SpaceX** 举办的安全峰会、**Elon Musk** 后来创办 **OpenAI**、AI 实验室之间的信任问题，以及为什么他认为可执行的规则既需要国内技术机构，也需要某种形式的 **中美** 协调。他以英国 AI Safety Institute 为例，说明政府可以组织起真正有技术能力的团队，但跨国协调依然很难。

sections.headline: **Peter Yang** shares six takeaways from **Josh Shpigford** on solo AI building · **Peter Yang** 总结 **Josh Shpigford** 单人用 AI 做产品的 6 点经验
sections.body:
My top 6 takeaways from @Shpigford on how to build multiple products solo with AI agents:

1. Keep shipping even if the fear of embarrassment never goes away.

After 25 years as a solo builder, Josh still thinks "It's terrifying launching something. Every single time it's just like, what if zero people care?" But he ships early anyway: "The idea of spending months working on something before you put it out for other people to use, I think that's a real bad idea."

2. Charge from day one, and kill products that can’t pay for themselves.

For any product with built-in costs (e.g., hosting, LLM), Josh ships a paid version from day one. If the product can't cover its own costs, he doesn't hesitate to shut it down and refund recent payments.

3. Build features in parallel with separate git worktrees

Each worktree is a separate working copy of your codebase on its own branch, so features won't interact with each other. Worktrees stop context rot, isolate mistakes, and force you to test every chunk before moving on. Josh uses @conductor_build to manage them all.

4. Have GPT review Claude's work and vice versa

Josh builds with one model and then runs a review pass with another “GPT invariably finds three to five bugs that Opus overlooked.” Different models spot different mistakes. In Conductor, he sets a default review model so it runs on every PR.

5. Build a skill to make AI better over time.

Josh built a /learnings skill that runs at the end of each phase so that every "no, that didn't work" moment can be distilled into new rules to help the agent avoid repeating the same mistakes.

6. AI lets anyone ship, but real experience still matters.

Josh credits 25 years of building before AI for how fast he ships now with agents. "I know the general shape of how I want things to work, so I can very quickly get to that point." His advice for newer builders is to "just fail a lot, because the only way that you'll ever figure out what not to do is by doing the thing incorrectly."

Josh walked through his entire development workflow in our episode and shared more skills.

📌 Watch the full episode here: https://t.co/9brwr7daw8

我从 @Shpigford 关于如何单人用 AI agents 做多个产品里，最想带走的 6 点：

1. 哪怕怕丢脸的感觉一直都在，也要继续发布。

做了 25 年 solo builder 之后，**Josh** 仍然觉得“发布东西很吓人。每一次都会想，要是没人关心怎么办？”但他还是会早早发布：“花几个月做东西，然后才拿给别人用，我觉得这是个很糟糕的主意。”

2. 第一天就收费，养不活自己的产品就关掉。

对任何有内置成本的产品，比如托管、LLM，**Josh** 从第一天就发布付费版本。如果产品不能覆盖自己的成本，他会直接关掉，并退还最近的付款。

3. 用独立 git worktrees 并行做功能。

每个 worktree 都是代码库在独立分支上的一个独立工作副本，所以功能之间不会互相干扰。Worktrees 能减少上下文腐烂、隔离错误，并迫使你在继续之前测试每一块。**Josh** 用 @conductor_build 管理这些 worktrees。

4. 让 **GPT** 审 **Claude** 的工作，反过来也一样。

**Josh** 用一个模型构建，再用另一个模型做 review，“**GPT** 总能找到 **Opus** 漏掉的三到五个 bug。”不同模型会发现不同问题。在 **Conductor** 里，他设置了默认 review 模型，让它在每个 PR 上运行。

5. 做一个 skill，让 AI 越用越好。

**Josh** 做了一个 /learnings skill，在每个阶段结束时运行，把每一次“不是，这样不行”的时刻提炼成新规则，帮助 agent 避免重复同样的错误。

6. AI 让任何人都能发货，但真实经验仍然重要。

**Josh** 认为，他能现在用 agents 快速发货，离不开 AI 出现前 25 年的构建经验。“我知道大概要让东西怎么运行，所以可以很快到达那个点。”他给新 builder 的建议是：“多失败，因为你只有把事情做错，才会知道什么不该做。”

**Josh** 在我们的节目里完整演示了他的开发流程，并分享了更多 skills。

📌 看完整节目：https://t.co/9brwr7daw8

sections.headline: Enterprise advantage in the AI agent era comes from internal knowledge · AI agent 时代的企业优势来自内部知识
sections.body:
As we enter the era of AI agents, one of the defining questions is how you develop competitive advantage when your competitor has access to the same AI models and intelligence as you. 

The companies that are able to best harness their internal institutional knowledge, existing data assets, and domain-specific workflows -- connected with AI -- will be those that are able to stay ahead in the future.

Whether a company decides to build out the tech stacks themselves, or leverage a variety of best-in-class tools is certainly one core variable. But the key is to find the way that the enterprise can capture and protect the value created by their unique data, processes, and expertise over the long run. Each industry will have their own version of this, and the competitive advantage will vary by vertical.

We’re increasingly seeing this at Box, where customers want to ensure that they can take advantage of their institutional knowledge and have the flexibility of bringing any AI model and intelligence to their data at any time. This is a pattern that will increasingly become a core principle of strategy in the future.

随着我们进入 AI agents 时代，一个核心问题是：当竞争对手能访问和你一样的 AI 模型与智能时，你怎么建立竞争优势。

那些最能利用内部组织知识、既有数据资产和行业专属工作流，并把它们与 AI 连接起来的公司，未来会更容易领先。

公司是自己搭技术栈，还是使用各种 best-in-class 工具，当然是一个关键变量。但真正的关键，是企业能不能长期捕获并保护由自身独特数据、流程和专业知识创造出的价值。每个行业都会有自己的版本，竞争优势也会因垂直领域而不同。

我们在 **Box** 越来越常看到这种模式：客户希望能利用自己的组织知识，同时保留灵活性，在任何时候把任意 AI 模型和智能接入自己的数据。这种模式会越来越成为未来战略的核心原则。
